source.title: On High-Dimensional Asymptotic Properties of Model Averaging Estimators

record.tranche_reason: Tests risk behavior in high-dimensional linear model-averaging estimators using random-matrix analysis and numerical experiments, rather than testing deep networks with the original method.
record.gate_note: The paper analyzes and simulates out-of-sample risk for linear model-averaging estimators. Its reported diagonal-component behavior directly bears on risk around the interpolation threshold. Several other reported results concern only off-diagonal risk components or relative performance against a min-norm estimator, so they do not establish a full double-descent curve.
record.test_reason: The paper derives asymptotic risk for averaged min-norm linear estimators (Theorem 2.1). Each component's risk blows up where model dimension equals sample size and falls beyond it. The authors state double descent occurs. This is a new estimator class bearing on V4, though it is mostly theory with only component-level plots.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right but incomplete. The authors derive high-dimensional asymptotic risk for model-averaging estimators built from min-norm least squares, including the misspecified and random-subset ensemble cases. They obtain optimal weights by directly minimizing asymptotic out-of-sample risk, and show double descent occurs in these estimators under certain conditions.
record.recipe_differences: High-dimensional linear regression with model averaging and min-norm least-squares component estimators; random-matrix risk analysis and simulations, rather than the original deep-network settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported risk behavior varies with candidate-model dimension, feature overlap, whether models are misspecified, feature-subset fraction, and whether samples are also randomly subsampled.

fits_no_version.finding: The off-diagonal risk component h12 improves as candidate-model dimension exceeds the sample size, and rises with feature overlap between candidate models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In linear model averaging, the cross-model risk term depends on candidate dimension and feature overlap.

fits_no_version.finding: In the misspecified case, the cross term h_mis,12 decreases and then gradually increases as Model 2 grows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In misspecified model averaging, the off-diagonal risk contribution is non-monotone in candidate size.

fits_no_version.finding: With many random-feature subsets, the ensemble risk equals the min-norm risk when each subset dimension exceeds n, and improves when it is below n. Subsampling samples as well (η=0.6) gives no improvement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of random-subset linear ensembles depends on subset sizes relative to n.

record.problems: Numerical results are mostly presented as plots without numeric point values or reported uncertainty. Several plotted quantities are off-diagonal risk components rather than full predictive risk. The tested estimators are linear, and the text does not establish the full generality of the curve across model classes.

untested.parts: Only linear min-norm and model-averaging estimators are covered. No other model classes are tested, no plot of the full combined risk curve over capacity is shown, and the classical U-shape in the under-parameterized regime is not examined.
No sweep of total sample size. The sample fraction η enters the formulas, but its effect on risk near the threshold is not reported.
σ² appears in the formulas, but no noise or regularization sweep is run. The ridge parameter λ→0 is used only as a proof device.

missing.what: Closed-form asymptotic risk for the model-averaging estimator, which diverges at γi=ηi and decreases for γi>ηi; this is the study's own double-descent evidence.
missing.locator: Section 2.1, Theorem 2.1, eq. (10)-(11); also Theorem 2.3 eq. (13) and Theorem 2.6 D term

record.verdict_notes: This is a theory-heavy preprint. Its simulations plot only off-diagonal components and ensemble risk, never the full averaged risk over capacity. The authors' 'double descent' label on the misspecified cross term (Figures 5-6) is loose. The V4 support rests on the derived formulas, which extend Hastie et al. (2022).

versions.untested_parts: Deep-network model-size sweep and the claimed fall-rise-fall shape.
Risk over training epochs or other training-time sweep.
Increasing the total training sample size near the interpolation threshold and measuring its effect on test risk.

Only high-dimensional linear and linear model-averaging estimators are considered; the study does not test the generality of the curve across broader model classes or establish the complete classical U-shaped-to-second-descent curve.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across axes.
No sweep tests label-noise dependence, multiple peaks, or disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
No alternative effective-parameter count is used to test whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: min-norm least-squares estimator (diagonal component of the model-averaging estimator)
rows.operation_detail: Compared the diagonal risk component with the stated min-norm least-squares risk behavior around the sample-dimension threshold.

conditions.value: diagonal component; discussed in numerical-experiment section

rows.value: Risk increases until the sample-to-dimension ratio exceeds 1, then decreases.
rows.note: The paper says the diagonal component behaves like min-norm least squares. This reports a rise to the threshold followed by a decrease; it does not report a preceding decline in this stated result.
rows.check: This is a cited result, not the study's own measurement. The text describes the diagonal component as behaving like min-norm least squares 'as shown in Hastie et al. (2022)', and no figure plots it. The paper's own evidence for V4 is the Theorem 2.1 formula, which no row records.

relationships.condition: Isotropic Gaussian linear regression; model-averaging estimator built from min-norm least-squares candidate models (asymptotic theory)
relationships.reason: Based on the text, not on any row. In Theorem 2.1, h_ii ~ γi/(ηi−γi) diverges as γi→ηi. For γi>ηi it equals (1−ηi/γi)r² + σ²ηi/(γi−ηi), which falls again. So risk peaks at the interpolation point and descends past it. The authors conclude double descent occurs under certain conditions.
relationships.display_finding: The theoretical risk term diverged as γi approached ηi and declined beyond interpolation under the stated conditions.
